meaning:
πλάνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX: Pro.14:8 (מִרְמָה), Wis.1:12, al ;]
a wandering. Metaphorical, a going astray, an error (in NT always with respect to morals or religion): Mat.27:64, Rom.1:27, Eph.4:14, 1Th.2:3, 2Th.2:11, Jas.5:20, 2Pe.2:18 3:17 3:1-18; 1Jn.4:6, Ju 11.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Command therefore that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come at night and steal him away, and tell the people, ‘He is…
Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and…
that we may no longer be children, tossed back and forth and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in craftiness, after the wiles…
For our exhortation is not of error, nor of uncleanness, nor in deception.
Because of this, God sends them a working of error, that they should believe a lie;
let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
For, uttering great swelling words of emptiness, they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by licentiousness, those who are indeed escaping from those who live in…
We are of God. He who knows God listens to us. He who is not of God doesn’t listen to us. By this we know the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.
